key_insight: On a fixed compact manifold, parallel transport convolution is continuous in L² under C² perturbations of the Riemannian metric, subject to the stated localization and transport-path conventions.
engineering_relevance: This provides a theoretical basis for robustness to small geometric changes in manifold-based convolution models, rather than an empirical performance guarantee.
method: Derive perturbation estimates for geodesics, parallel transport, Jacobi fields, and exponential maps.
Compare transported kernels using uniform estimates away from the cut locus and integral bounds near it.
Control changes in the Riemannian volume measure.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a qualitative stability theorem for continuous signals and continuous reference kernels with sufficiently small normal-neighborhood support, not numerical experiments or benchmarks.
watch_item: The theorem gives no quantitative robustness rate, and implementations must respect the localization and transport-path assumptions.
paper_title: Stability of Parallel Transport Convolution under Riemannian Metric Perturbations
